layers.note: A herb of wet meadows, fens and stream banks, in scattered groups; a root hemiparasite.

moisture.note: Wet ground: boggy meadows, seeps and stream margins.

elevation_m.note: Near sea level in the boreal north to about 3,700 m in the southern Rockies.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −25 to 1 °C; gone below −35 °C and above 5 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −45 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −52 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 7 to 18 °C; gone below 5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 21 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 600 to 3,200 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: About 150 to 1,700 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 50.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.5, gone by 0.35.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Elephant's head grows across boreal Canada and from Alaska to California and New Mexico, in wet meadows and bogs (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
